summary: Hold: 1.16.2 is a small, zero-dependency, MIT-licensed Node transport with recent releases and no recorded advisories, but the dossier shows no npm provenance and no publish-pipeline facts, so the release-integrity half of the rubric is unverified and the package is only acceptable in the axios stack with exact pinning and a recorded gap.
reasoning: Purpose and fit: the request names follow-redirects as part of the axios stack, where it is reached transitively rather than imported by application code; the review therefore asks whether it is acceptable to keep in that stack, not whether it should be added as a direct dependency.

Footprint is minimal for this requirement: 0 runtime dependencies, an empty dependencies object, 31 KB unpacked, and an empty install_scripts list, so it adds no install-time execution and no transitive tree to the axios stack.
Security surface as recorded: the dossier's vulnerabilities array is empty for 1.16.2 and no warnings were emitted during collection, so there is no known unfixed advisory to cap the verdict.
Maintenance looks active: 1.16.2 was published 2026-10-25, the repository was pushed 2026-10-25, it is not archived, and 73 versions have been published by two npm maintainers.

Release integrity is the gap: npm_provenance is false and the provenance note says no npm attestation was found, and the dossier contains no workflow or release-job facts, so CI publishing cannot be confirmed or denied from the measured evidence.
The requirement explicitly allows an npm provenance gap only if exact versions are pinned and the gap is recorded; this review records the gap but cannot verify that pinning is enforced downstream.
Fit is constrained by packaging: types is "none" and formats is ["cjs"], so TypeScript consumers get no declarations from the package and ESM projects rely on CommonJS interop.
The 93,968,125 weekly downloads are recorded but not treated as a quality signal: download counts include CI and transitive installs, and the dossier does not attribute them to direct use.

The dossier does not measure install size (install_size_kb is null) and does not exercise redirect behaviour, so footprint and runtime behaviour conclusions are limited to the 31 KB unpacked figure and registry metadata.
caveats: No npm attestation for 1.16.2: the requirement permits this only with exact version pinning and a recorded provenance gap. Pin 1.16.2 exactly and re-check provenance on each upgrade.
CI publishing was not measured in the dossier. If a human review finds that releases are cut manually, the no-CI-publishing hard failure applies and the verdict should drop to avoid.
No bundled TypeScript declarations (types: "none") and CJS-only output; TypeScript and ESM consumers need their own typings strategy and interop checks.
The dossier provides no browser or bundler evidence; treat this as the Node-side transport in the axios stack rather than a browser HTTP client.
Install size was not measured (null); only the 31 KB unpacked figure is available, so total cost in the axios tree is unknown from this dossier.
Two npm maintainers and 21 open issues on a repository with 581 stars: small enough that responsiveness to a future advisory depends on a short cadence, not on depth of maintainer bench.
Historical advisories are not represented in the dossier's empty vulnerabilities list, so the empty result should not be read as a claim that the package has never had a redirect-handling issue.
